title: Making a fitted loose cover for a dining chair seat
subtitle: Cut and sew a fitted fabric cover for a drop-in dining chair seat that slips off for washing and fits back cleanly
excerpt: How to make a fitted loose cover for a drop-in dining chair seat. Covers cutting a pattern from the seat, sewing the face panels with fitted corners, and adding ties or elastic to hold the cover in place.
sourceNotes: UK upholstery and soft-furnishing trade practice. City and Guilds upholstery syllabi (open access).

glossaryTerms.definition: A method of fitting fabric around the corner of a seat cushion cover without puckering. A small fold of fabric is pleated at 90 degrees at each corner, giving a crisp, box-like appearance. Used on fitted loose covers and on box cushion covers.
The extra fabric width added beyond the seam stitch line, typically 12-15 mm in upholstery work. The seam allowance is trimmed or notched at curves after stitching to allow the seam to lie flat.

content.text: A fitted loose cover slips over the drop-in seat and ties or elastics under the chair frame, so it can come off for washing. The job is cut a pattern, sew the face and skirt panels together with
, and fit ties to the underside. Allow a

Remove the drop-in seat from the chair. Lay it face-down on the fabric and draw around it with chalk or a pencil, adding 15 mm seam allowance all round. This is the top panel. The skirt panels are cut to the depth of the seat edge plus 30 mm (for a hem at the base and a seam at the top). Measure the perimeter of the seat top at the edge; cut four skirt panels to match each side, or one continuous strip for the front and two sides.
Sew the skirt to the top panel

Stitch the skirt panels together at the corners with box pleats: at each corner, fold a small inverted pleat in the skirt strip (a 25 mm inverted tuck) and pin. Check the fit around the seat before sewing. Sew the top panel to the skirt with a 15 mm seam allowance, right sides together, clipping the seam allowance at curves. Turn right side out and press.
Fit the cover to the seat

Slip the cover over the seat. It should sit snugly with the seam line at the edge. Fold the base hem under the seat and pin four fabric tie loops or sew a channel for elastic around the base edge. Fabric ties in pairs at each corner hold the cover under the chair; elastic pulled through a hem channel gives a tighter, self-adjusting fit.

attrs.symptom: Cover slips forward or lifts when someone sits down
attrs.cause: Ties or elastic not holding securely enough under the seat base.
attrs.fix: Use wider ties or pass them around the chair leg rather than just under the seat base. Add two extra ties at the back corners.

attrs.symptom: Box pleat corners pucker at the seam line
attrs.cause: The pleat depth was not equal on both sides of the corner.
attrs.fix: Unpick the corner seam, equalise the pleat folds, re-press and re-sew.
